Root key: metrics-credentials. One direct executable child: metrics-credential-transition. No prerequisite.

Objective: concurrent Gateway operations on one Metrics Node cannot commit a credential based on stale state or restore settings deleted by a competing purge. Existing pending-password recovery, authentication, and secret handling remain intact.

Scope:

- In: the credential manager's initialization, reset, purge, and necessary verified-read boundaries; a narrow Metrics operation lock; its dependency binding; focused Gateway tests and reproducible machine observation; the maintained Metrics reference and its generated context.
- Out: full Metrics runtime or publication serialization; role architecture changes; schema migration; changing Grafana access or exporter policy; new SDK or CLI behavior; queues, generic workflow frameworks, or Incus harness implementation changes.
- Normal removal still preserves passwords and data. Explicit forced purge still deletes only proven-owned Metrics data and the active/pending settings. A later newly authorized enable can initialize new credentials; preventing all future initialization after a purge is not the requested contract.

Shared context:

- Repository paths below are relative to the assigned Orbit checkout. They must travel with the root/child brief, not depend on this conversation or the temporary author directory.
- `AGENTS.md`, `apps/gateway/AGENTS.md`, and `apps/gateway/.ai/rules/index.md` define the project and guidance bootstrap. Use matching app, infrastructure, tests, and binding rules. G1 is resolved as an evaluator setup error; the required bootstrap still applies to the later assigned worktree.
- `docs/decisions/0003-singleton-metrics-role.md` governs encrypted per-Node active/pending credentials, verified promotion, explicit purge, and Gateway-owned synchronous operations.
- `docs/decisions/0055-restrict-grafana-access-to-authorized-gateway-peers.md` preserves Grafana login and credential controls. ORB-229 is Done and explicitly excluded credential lifecycle; its Gateway authorization and upstream isolation must remain unchanged.
- `docs/reference/metrics.md` describes current credential commands, no-store responses, normal removal, purge, and recovery. Update its credential section, not unrelated access/exporter material.
- `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md`, `docs/decisions/0059-make-the-builder-own-the-candidate-quality-gate.md`, and `docs/reference/incus-topologies.md` govern TIA, exact-candidate checks, discovery observations, and exclusive topology commands. ADR 0059 owns the Builder gate despite stale reviewer-owned wording in Gateway test guidance.
- `apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/Metrics/NativeMetricsCredentialManager.php` currently reads/generates active credentials without an owner. Reset reads and writes pending, calls remote apply/verify, then only wraps final promotion/deletion in a DB transaction. Purge's transaction does not exclude those earlier reads or remote work.
- `apps/gateway/app/Domain/Settings/SettingRepository.php` rereads persisted encrypted settings per call; retain that property after ownership is acquired.
- `apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/Metrics/NativeMetricsContainerRuntime.php` calls initialization before rendering/publishing and calls `verifyActive` after container convergence. Removal purges owned volumes before credential settings. The requested lock is not ownership of that entire runtime interval.
- `apps/gateway/app/Actions/Nodes/AssignRoleAction.php`, `AddNodeRoleAction.php`, and `RemoveNodeRoleAction.php` use short role-claim transactions before remote convergence/removal. Do not introduce waiting for a credential lock while holding those database locks, or a reverse lock acquisition path.
- `apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/AppDev/NativeDevelopmentProjectionOperationLock.php` is an inspected example of non-expiring `flock` ownership with bounded acquisition and `finally` release. `apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/Processes/CommandDeadline.php` caps waits against the remaining API deadline. Reuse the proven invariants, not the unrelated projection lock key or global scope.
- `apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/Metrics/MetricsSshExecutor.php` uses protected inputs and authenticated Grafana verification. Neither `/api/health` alone nor a successful transport call proves password validity.
- `apps/gateway/app/Http/Controllers/Api/MetricsController.php` preserves Gateway access middleware, response envelope, and `Cache-Control: no-store`; no frontend changes are needed.

## Coverage and order

The single-child chain is deliberate: separating a small lock helper from its credential consumer would add an assignment without producing an independently useful supported behavior. Code, tests, and operator guidance establish one invariant in one commit.

| Original issue item | Root criterion | Child criteria | Final checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1: competing resets, purge, first creation | F1 | T1, T2, T3 | I1, I2, I5 |
| 2: pending retry and verified promotion | F2 | T2, T4 | I1, I2, I5 |
| 3: release, secrets, fresh reads | F3 | T1, T2, T3, T4 | I1, I2, I5 |
| 4: real-machine boundary | F4 | T5 | I2, I5 |
| 5: maintained/generated documentation | F5 | T6 | I3, I5 |
| 6: Gateway checks | F6 | T2, T3, T4 | I1, I4, I5 |
| 7: generic repository suites | F7 | combined child output | I4, I5 |

Original item 7 is aligned to current TIA/Builder policy, not dropped. Items 6/7 move from the issue description into the package's explicit required policy gates. Original item 4 maps to reproducible discovery observations, not an unselected immutable proof flow. The full proposed issue payload remains unpublished until separately approved.

### Final feature acceptance

- F1: Reset/reset, reset/purge, and first-creation contention serialize the relevant state transitions. No operation promotes a stale pending snapshot, generates a competing initial password from stale absence, or restores settings using a snapshot taken before purge. Subsequent operations reread authoritative state under ownership.
- F2: Failures before apply, after apply, and during authentication retain recoverable encrypted pending state. Retry verifies whether Grafana already holds pending, avoids needless reapply when it does, and promotes only authenticated pending values.
- F3: Contention has a bounded refusal path with no protected mutation by the refused operation. Ownership cannot expire while the owner is executing; exceptions release it. Node keys isolate unrelated credential operations. No database transaction spans SSH or lock acquisition. Passwords remain absent from argv, exception/debug text, ordinary responses, and logs; explicit credential responses retain no-store and existing authorization.
- F4: Real Gateway processes and real Grafana exhibit F1–F3 on issue-owned Incus discovery, with zero-exit behavior assertions and retained, redacted evidence. Setup readiness alone is insufficient.
- F5: The maintained Metrics reference accurately describes the changed contention, retry, and purge contract. Generated documentation context is current and documentation lint passes.
- F6: Gateway affected tests and quality checks pass, including regression coverage for the preserved API, runtime, and protected-input behavior.
- F7: The clean committed integrated candidate passes the Builder's root `composer check` across all five Composer projects; a separate exact-candidate integrated review validates its receipt, combined acceptance, and machine evidence before the root can complete. Passing the child alone does not satisfy this criterion.

### Final integrated checks

These checks are planned, not run in preparation. Commander must retain the exact candidate, commands, exit statuses, logs, and independent verdict.

- I1: F1–F3/F6; assigned worktree `apps/gateway`; `composer test:affected`, then `composer check`; expect exit 0 and actual affected behavior coverage. Existing commands; new contention tests belong to the child. No Pest path/filter/group/suite selection. TIA selecting zero tests is not fresh acceptance evidence.
- I2: F4 and real-machine F1–F3; issue-owned discovery; first inspect restored source, role assignment, Grafana health, encrypted-setting presence without printing secrets, and actual Node/SSH/network identity. Then run the child's planned `metrics-credential-contention` fixture via the existing `bin/e2e-topology exec` interface. Expect asserted races and recovery cases to exit 0, with the owner's and contender's observed outcomes and credential-state assertions recorded. Preserve supported normal-remove/purge behavior. Record corrections, guest changes, and cleanup.
- I3: F5; repository root; `composer docs-build` then `composer docs-lint`; expect current generated context and exit 0. Existing commands. Retain any generated source changes in the reviewed snapshot; do not regenerate after final commit without a new snapshot/candidate.
- I4: F1–F7; clean committed integrated worktree root; Builder/final-check assignment runs `composer check`; expect successful exact-candidate/tree receipt with all five project outcomes. Existing command; the corrected preparation guidance check is not a passing candidate gate, so no candidate result is assumed. Commander validates the receipt before integrated candidate review; independent reviewer validates it without repeating the full gate solely to approve.
- I5: F1–F7; independent integrated reviewer checks the exact committed candidate, I1–I4 evidence, scope, documentation, and the acceptance map; expect explicit pass. This is distinct from the child snapshot review that authorizes its commit. Any source correction needs a new reviewed snapshot, candidate gate, and integrated verdict.

The flow is proposed as default discovery, not proof selected by the `incus` label. Preserve a pre-existing explicit flow if admission finds one; a conflicting flow requires preparation revision. For discovery report `Discovery development only; isolated acceptance proof not run`. No worktree, topology, snapshot, or runtime is created by this package. After independent preparation passes and admission is separately authorized, normal setup uses `bin/e2e-topology acquire ORB-170 WORKTREE`; all topology commands are sequential, including commands aimed at different Nodes. A single guest fixture may create and await competing processes to exercise the race without concurrent host topology commands. Harness repairs require separate scoped work.

issue.title: Serialize metrics credential transitions under one owner
issue.description:
Metrics credential initialization, reset, and purge have one operation owner per Node, so competing transitions cannot promote stale credentials or restore purged settings. The credential lifecycle follows [ADR 0003](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-singleton-metrics-role.md>).

## Scope
